learningObjective: Understand generation-by-generation Tensor Core dtype support and portability implications.

canonicalClaims.claim: NVIDIA Tensor Core dtype support grew generation-by-generation: Volta FP16 → Turing INT8 → Ampere TF32/BF16/FP64 → Ada/Hopper FP8. Kernels using specific dtypes require the matching compute capability.
nonImplications: Does not imply future architectures will keep all past dtypes.
Does not imply per-dtype throughput ratios are stable.

misconceptions.claim: All Tensor Core dtypes are available from Volta onwards.
misconceptions.whyWrong: BF16/TF32 arrived with Ampere; FP8 with Ada/Hopper.

misconceptions.claim: FP8 is available on Ampere GPUs.
BF16/TF32/FP8 are software emulations on FP16 hardware.
Tensor Core throughput per dtype is identical across generations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Peak MMA rates change per architecture; FP32 accumulator handling differs.

implementationFacts: sm_70: FP16; sm_75: +INT8; sm_80: +TF32/BF16/FP64; sm_89: +FP8; sm_90: FP8 formalized with new throughput.
